subject: Pre-deployment load verification & go/no-go window — ParcelGrid
messages:
From: Sara Kaplan <sara.kaplan@parcelgrid.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Oct 2028 14:05:00 -0400
Subject: ParcelGrid onboarding — load test targets and windows

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. ParcelGrid is ready to move into the pre-prod verification phase. Before we lock calendar slots, can you confirm the runbook you plan to use for benchmarking and the acceptance thresholds we should expect? Our engineering lead (Tim) and procurement are looped.

Key asks from our side:
- Clear target numbers for throughput and tail latency (p50/p95/p99) for a sustained workload
- The test dataset and any API/key requirements (we can provide a scrubbed sample)
- Proposed dates/times for a 2–3 hour verification window next week (we're aiming for Oct 23 or 24)

We need go/no-go confirmation for our internal signoff by Oct 25.

Appreciate a short plan you can share.

Best,
Sara Kaplan
Senior Product Manager
ParcelGrid

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sara Kaplan <sara.kaplan@parcelgrid.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Oct 2028 16:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: ParcelGrid onboarding — load test targets and windows

Sara — thanks, and great meeting yesterday. Looping in CS and implementation. Attached are the initial test plan and the Redwood test matrix that we run for onboarding playtests. High level plan below:

1) Baseline: 10 minutes of warmup at low concurrency to validate correctness and cold-start behavior
2) Concurrency sweep: step up to target QPS in 30% increments, holding at each phase for 5–10 minutes to collect p50/p95/p99 and CPU/GPU telemetry
3) Sustained run: 30 minutes at expected production QPS to validate throughput and memory/kv-cache stability
4) Tail-latency stress: short bursts to capture p99+ tail behavior and retry surface

Preliminary acceptance thresholds (we'll finalize with engineering):
- Sustained throughput target: 200–300 qps (depends on payload size)
- p50 < 100 ms, p95 < 350 ms, p99 < 800 ms (these are starting targets; we'll tighten after the baseline)

We can run the test window Oct 23 02:00–05:00 UTC (Oct 23 local US evening) or Oct 24 same window — which would you prefer?

Attachments: parcelgrid_loadplan_v1.xlsx, redwood-test-matrix.md

Next steps:
- ParcelGrid provides scrubbed sample payload (or S3 link) and a contact for temporary test credentials
- We will provision an ephemeral key via our secure vault and share instructions (no secrets in email)
- Post-run we'll share detailed telemetry and a results packet

If that all sounds good I'll lock the Oct 23 slot and notify infra.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Customer Implementation, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Sara Kaplan <sara.kaplan@parcelgrid.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Oct 2028 09:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: ParcelGrid onboarding — load test targets and windows

Thanks — quick operational note from CS/ops side:

To make the go/no-go decision straightforward we recommend these concrete acceptance criteria for the playtest (we can relax/adjust if ParcelGrid expects much larger payloads):
- Sustained throughput: >= 250 qps for 30 minutes
- p50 < 80 ms, p95 < 300 ms, p99 < 700 ms
- No more than 2% error-rate (product-level errors, not transient throttles)
- Memory/kv-cache stable — no OOMs or sustained >85% GPU memory utilization

Also please provide:
- A 10–15k record sanitized payload (or a representative sampling)
- A clear success-case example response for correctness checks

We'll prepare the runbook and provide test access instructions. We'll send the credential provisioning steps separately (attachment: test-credentials-instructions.txt).

Ben Carter
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Sara Kaplan <sara.kaplan@parcelgrid.com>, Tim Olson <tim.olson@parcelgrid.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Oct 2028 18:20:00 -0400
Subject: Re: ParcelGrid onboarding — load test targets and windows — results and next steps

Team — thank you. We completed the Oct 23 playtest in the agreed window. Summary of results (detailed artifacts attached):

Artifacts attached: load-results-20281023.json, telemetry-snapshot-20281023.tar.gz

Key findings:
- Sustained throughput: 265 qps for 30 minutes (payload average 1.2kB) — PASS against 250 qps threshold
- Latency: p50 = 72 ms, p95 = 290 ms, p99 = 650 ms — PASS against the acceptance bands Ben suggested
- Error rate: 0.8% (largely transient 429s during the concurrency ramp; no product-level faults)
- Observations: increased tail latency during short high-concurrency bursts linked to small KV cache misses; GPU utilization peaked at 78% with headroom.

Recommendations and next steps:
1) Canary: proceed to a small production canary with quantized model variant (saves ~30% token cost) and prefix caching enabled — target canary start Oct 27
2) Operational tweak: enable a slightly larger warm-up hold for concurrency ramps to reduce 429s during step-ups; infra scheduled an autoscale policy tweak to reduce transient throttles
3) Deliverables: full telemetry packet (attached), annotated runbook with observed failure modes, and a short-run remediation checklist for ParcelGrid on-call

If ParcelGrid is comfortable, we'll prepare the canary rollout plan and a short post-canary acceptance check to confirm no regressions. Otherwise, if you'd like additional stress tests (e.g., larger payloads or longer sustained window) we can schedule a follow-up.

Thanks — nice collaboration.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Customer Implementation, Redwood Inference

Redwood Inference
